biography: Henri Greder's journey to racing began not on a track, but on the winding, sun-drenched roads of the French Riviera. Growing up near Nice, Henri spent his youth tearing around on a beat-up moped, much to the chagrin of the local gendarmes. His raw talent was undeniable, transforming a youthful obsession into a serious pursuit when he won a local karting championship at 17. Transitioning to saloon cars, Greder quickly gained a reputation for daring overtakes and a 'never say die' attitude. While his early career was marked by frequent crashes and mechanical failures, his sheer tenacity caught the eye of Chevrolet's European racing division. Now, at 29, Greder is at the peak of his powers, a force to be reckoned with in endurance racing, known for pushing his machinery to the absolute limit – sometimes beyond.
drivingStyle: Greder's driving style is a high-risk, high-reward approach. He's known for late braking maneuvers that often leave rivals shaking their heads in disbelief. Tire management isn't exactly his forte; he prefers to extract every last ounce of performance from the rubber, even if it means a drastic drop-off in the closing laps. Under pressure, Greder thrives, often finding an extra gear when the stakes are highest. He's a master of controlled aggression, always teetering on the edge of disaster but rarely crossing the line.
rivalries: Jean-Pierre Dubois - A clash of generations, with the veteran Dubois criticizing Greder's aggressive tactics as reckless and immature.
Isabelle Moreau - A fierce on-track battle for position at Le Mans resulted in a controversial collision and lingering animosity.
Marco Bellini - Bellini, a calculated and precise driver, openly disapproves of Greder's 'unprofessional' driving standards, leading to frequent clashes both on and off the track.
quirks: Always wears a lucky vintage racing glove on his left hand, a relic from his grandfather's own short-lived racing career.
Listens to classic French jazz before every race to calm his nerves, a stark contrast to the roar of the engines.
Refuses to eat anything green on race day, a superstition stemming from a disastrous race where he ate a salad and suffered a mechanical failure.
famousQuote: "Racing isn't about playing it safe; it's about finding that edge, that moment of pure adrenaline, and holding on for dear life."
careerHighlight: Winning the Spa 24 Hours in 2022, battling through torrential rain and several mechanical setbacks to secure a last-lap victory by a mere two seconds.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead at the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2021 due to a mechanical failure with less than an hour remaining, costing his team a potential victory.
